results.content: This study adopted a mixed-methods design to assess the reliability and validity of the "Chinese version of the Postoperative Anticoagulation Motivation Scale for Deep Vein Thrombosis Prophylaxis in Patients After Arthroplasty," based on Protection Motivation Theory, conducted sequentially in two stages. Several fit indices were used to evaluate the adequacy of the models, including normalized chi-square (CMIN/DF), root mean square error of approximation (RMSEA), parsimonious normative fit index (PNFI), relative fit index (RFI), incremental fit index (IFI), Tucker–Lewis fit index (TLI), and parsimony goodness-of-fit index (PGFI).The CFA results indicated that the motivational scale for anticoagulant use in DVT prophylaxis based on Protection Motivation Theory achieved an acceptable but not optimal fit for the five-factor model (Model 2), with RMSEA=0.076, IFI=0.896, and TLI=0.888 (Table 5). This careful development process ensures that the scale effectively and efficiently assesses the motivation of patients on anticoagulant medication for deep vein thrombosis prophylaxis after arthroplasty, and it has strong scientific validity. ### Reliability and validity of the motivation scale for medication protection for Deep Vein thrombosis prophylaxis in post-arthroplasty patients. Factors influencing medication adherence for deep vein thrombosis prevention in post-discharge patients after joint replacement surgery: a qualitative study based on protection motivation theory.
